summary: René Grousset worked in sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Montpellier (~1903–1906) and held posts at the Musée Guimet, Louvre Museum, École du Louvre, and Musée Cernuschi.

René Guénon worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the Robert-Badinter School Complex (1902–1903), Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1904–1906), and the University of Paris (1914–1917).

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz specialized in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Berlin, Vienna (under Koppers, Haekel, and Bleichsteiner), SOAS, and LSE, also learning from Tucci and Rock. In 1958, he was a wissenschaftlicher Beamter at Weltmuseum Wien.
Reting Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Chatral Sangye Dorje, and he taught Tenzin Gyatso.

Rewata Dhamma was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and ~1967, and earned a doctorate from Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

Richard A. Hutch worked in religious studies. He studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago, later holding posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).
Richard B. Martin specialized in Indology and Tibetology. He served at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and as a South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and with Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center, serving as abbot (1971–1984), and founded Dharma Sangha.
Richard Barron specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bowring is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge (BA, doctorate, Litt.D), he held posts at Columbia and Princeton before serving as Cambridge's Professor of Japanese Studies (1985) and Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

Richard Carnac Temple worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Harrow and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, he served in the Indian Army and Bengal Staff Corps, was proprietor of Indian Antiquary (~1884–1931), and vice-president of the Hakluyt Society.
Richard D. Mann specializes in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He was a graduate student at UCLA under mentor Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and worked at Dongguk University.

Richard Delbrueck was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1894–1899), where he later held a post (~1908–1911), followed by positions at the University of Giessen and University of Jena.

Richard F. Nance is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (-2004) and served as Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University (attested 2013).

Richard Fick worked in Indology. After earning his doctorate at Kiel University (1885–1888), he held posts at Kiel's library, the Prussian State Library, Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932), and the University of Göttingen (1923).

Richard Foltz works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history. Educated at the University of Utah and Harvard University, he taught at Brown, Columbia, and Florida, and became Founding Director at Concordia University (~2006–2026).
Richard Fritzsche specialized in Indology. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus and held a post as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.

Richard Gombrich is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, Walpola Rahula, and Gananath Obeyesekere, he served as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1965–2004) and held a post at Balliol College.

Richard Hartshorne studied at Princeton University (~1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1920–1924). He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).
